source.title: On Dropout and Nuclear Norm Regularization

record.file_problem: Full paper text and supplementary proofs are present; no apparent truncation or garbling that prevents extraction.
record.tranche_reason: The paper tests dropout-related regularization properties in deep linear networks, including empirical measurements of shrinkage and equalization. It does not test natural-label generalization or train/test error gaps directly, but its trained-network measurements bear on V7's measured properties.
record.gate_note: The paper's theory and experiments concern explicit and induced dropout regularization, singular-value shrinkage, and equalization in deep linear regression. It does not report natural-label versus random-label generalization, test error changes from dropout, or an empirical relationship between the measured equalization gaps and a train/test generalization gap. The row retained maps only to V7 as a measured property of trained networks; cited prior work and the theoretical regularizer results are not empirical rows.
record.test_reason: The study characterizes dropout regularization in deep linear regression. Its experiments measure spectral shrinkage and equalization, not dropout's effect on held-out classifier error (V6) or magnitude-aware sharpness versus generalization gaps (V7). Section 5 leaves dropout's role in generalization for future research.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is substantially correct. The authors characterize dropout's explicit regularizer as containing the squared l2-path regularizer and other rescaling-invariant terms. Its induced regularizer's convex envelope is an architecture- and dropout-dependent multiple of the squared nuclear norm of the network map multiplied by the input second-moment square root. They characterize global optima under an eigengap condition and empirically demonstrate spectral shrinkage and approximate equalization. They do not establish improved generalization.
record.recipe_differences: The paper studies deep linear regression with dropout and squared loss, rather than the natural-label classification generalization experiments in the claim versions. Its experiments use Gaussian inputs and generated linear labels.
record.method_sensitivity: Dropout rate changes the amount of singular-value shrinkage and the resulting network-map rank; the paper reports that effective regularization increases with dropout rate. The equalization-gap result is reported for one specified architecture.

fits_no_version.finding: Dropout training quickly decreases the normalized equalization gap and keeps the tested network approximately equalized.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: In the tested deep linear network with one output and five width-5 hidden layers, dropout training approaches the theoretical lower bound on its explicit regularizer.

fits_no_version.finding: Increasing dropout shrinks singular values more strongly and lowers the trained network map's rank (Section 4.1, Figure 2).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Dropout induces spectral shrinkage and rank control in the tested synthetic deep linear regression setting.

record.problems: The empirical study uses generated Gaussian regression data and does not measure generalization gaps or held-out classification error. The equalization result is shown for a single specified architecture; the figure gives no numerical values in the text.
record.rows_left_out: No eligible rows omitted. The spectrum shrinkage and thresholding results in Figure 2 do not measure a version's train/test generalization gap or another measured property named in V7. The theoretical regularizer characterization and cited prior results are not standalone empirical rows under the row criteria.

rows.measure: Normalized equalization gap r(t), defined as R({Wi})/Θ**(Wk+1→1) − 1.
rows.value: Figure 3 shows the gap decreasing; the text says the network quickly becomes approximately equalized and thereafter stays close to equalized networks.
rows.note: This measures equalization, not a train/test generalization gap; therefore it maps to no listed version.
rows.check: The reported equalization is observed, but cannot establish any listed version. Equalization compares the dropout regularizer with its theoretical lower bound; it is neither sharpness nor a train/test generalization gap. The equalized reference is r(t)=0. Section 4 reports 50 repetitions, with means and standard deviations, so uncertainty is available qualitatively.
